commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor console I/O into Ui class
commitResults.messageBody:
Extract the user-interaction code from the main chatbot loop into a dedicated Ui class.
This is the first incremental step toward the target OOP structure: Sage remains responsible for flow control and persistence, while the UI layer is isolated and easier to evolve independently.

- Added a dedicated Ui class for welcome banners, task list output, add/remove/mark feedback, and error messages.
- Updated Sage.java to delegate all console I/O to Ui.
- Verified the CLI behavior with the project UI regression suite.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor code to meet coding standards
Add GitHub Actions workflow for CI
commitResults.messageBody:
Automated builds and tests are required to verify code on pushes
and pull requests. Let's add a Gradle CI workflow configuration
file under .github/workflows/ to catch integration errors early.

Null pointers or invalid states can cause silent bugs during execution.
Let's add Java assertions to key classes like Parser and TaskList to
explicitly catch invalid runtime states early.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share task date parsing and display rules
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline and Event duplicated date formats, parsing fallbacks, and
midnight display rules. Updating one copy could leave the other with
different behavior, and nested exception handlers obscured the flow.

Extract TaskDateTime to keep those rules in one place and try each
format through a small helper. Preserve the existing public methods,
accepted formats, and fallback text.

This follows the code quality guidelines on minimizing duplication
and avoiding deep nesting. Add regression tests for every format,
blank and unsupported input, and fallback display behavior.

Validation: all 33 JUnit tests and all 10 CLI UI scenarios pass on
Java 25.

Parser.parse mixed command selection with every argument format and
validation rule. Its length made individual command behavior hard to
follow, while numeric substring offsets hid their meaning.

Extract focused parsers for task commands and share task-number
validation. Derive argument offsets from command and delimiter lengths
so those values cannot drift when their text changes.

This applies the guidelines on short methods, consistent abstraction,
and avoiding magic numbers. Preserve command matching, error messages,
and accepted date values with regression tests.

Validation: all 38 JUnit tests and all 10 CLI UI scenarios pass on
Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate task records from storage file access
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage mixed file operations with record parsing and serialization.
Repeated date formatting branches and unexplained field offsets made
the persisted format difficult to inspect and change safely.

Extract TaskCodec with named field positions and small methods for
task creation and stored-time formatting. Storage now delegates record
conversion while retaining its existing file and recovery behavior.

This follows the guidelines on logical structure, short methods,
consistent abstraction, and minimizing duplication. Add tests for
exact records, free-text times, malformed fields, blank lines, and
recovery when corruption follows a valid record.

Validation: all 45 JUnit tests and all 10 CLI UI scenarios pass on
Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Java Streams for task filtering
commitResults.messageBody:
Traditional loops make filtering collections verbose and repetitive.
Let's refactor the find feature to use Java Streams for cleaner,
more declarative collection processing.
Use Java Streams for task filtering

commitResults.messageTitle: Protect Sage data and handle common input errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Malformed commands and failed saves can confuse users or discard data.
Validate exact command names, time fields, dates, duplicates, and limits.
Preserve legacy records while safely escaping newly saved text.

Write complete temporary files before replacement, block saves after a
failed load, and restore in-memory state when persistence fails. Keep
search result numbers consistent with subsequent mutation commands.

Add regression tests and a portable, isolated CLI acceptance runner so
these guarantees can be checked without touching personal task data.

Long assistant replies need more space than short user commands, and
errors should be distinguishable without relying on colour alone.

Use compact command rows, full-width response cards, labelled errors,
responsive wrapping, and a resizable sage-green window. Keep failed
commands selected for correction and provide command help, recall,
copying, and clear keyboard focus without large profile pictures.

Verify packaged FXML and stylesheet references in headless tests.
Interactive rendering still requires a desktop smoke test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Give Sage a calm and practical personality
commitResults.messageBody:
The interface should feel consistent while keeping recovery advice clear
and useful. Replace alarm-style errors with gentle prompts, use a shared
welcome message, and describe progress in a calm, encouraging voice.

Add actionable empty-list guidance, readable entry numbering, and correct
singular and plural counts that include both tasks and notes. Match the
window subtitle to this identity and update exact response expectations.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make Sage releases portable and keep local data private
commitResults.messageBody:
A release must not depend on a developer checkout or accidentally mix
Intel and Apple Silicon JavaFX native libraries with identical names.

Follow the tutorial dependency layout and produce a separate ARM macOS
JAR. Verify launcher metadata, resources, native architecture, relocation,
Unicode persistence, and absence of personal files in release artifacts.
Configure Java 25 CI across supported desktop platforms and enforce
coverage checks for testable application logic.

Stop tracking personal task data and the machine-local visual tool while
preserving both locally. Document runtime requirements, release checks,
and platform-testing limitations without rewriting existing history.

commitResults.messageTitle: Expand automated coverage and document release evidence
commitResults.messageBody:
Successful command tests alone miss important storage, parsing, and
application-loop failures. Exercise malformed UTF-8, escaped fields,
precise date-time persistence, empty saves, and corrupted-file recovery.
Cover console continuation after errors and output-only UI contracts.

Accept harmless repeated whitespace inside numeric date-time input and
lock that behavior down with unit and exact-output acceptance tests.

Record 95 passing JUnit tests, 18 CLI scenarios per release, six runner
regressions, and 99.1 percent line coverage for non-GUI code. Keep manual
GUI and remote-platform checks explicitly pending instead of implying
that local automated results prove those environments were tested.

Replace screenshot placeholders with the supplied Sage window capture.
Keep the user guide, supporting technical documentation, and site assets
focused by removing redundant setup and screenshot scaffolding.

Consolidate publishing instructions in the release guide and check local
page links and rendering before handing publication to the maintainer.
Remove developer-facing release, testing, and assertion notes from the published site. Keep the user guide, screenshot, and website assets focused on end users.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix release validation and search edge cases
commitResults.messageBody:
Reject bare numbers, punctuation-only date labels, unsupported years,
and impossible AM/PM times so malformed input cannot enter saved lists.
Retain validation causes and test rejected commands, saved-file protection,
and successful recovery after correcting an input.

Normalize phrase spacing during search to match the duplicate-check rules.
Align the Apple Silicon CI artifact path and user guide with the current
JAR filename so release verification can find the generated archive.

Verify 104 JUnit tests, 20 CLI scenarios, Javadoc generation, and both
release archive variants with Java 25. All non-private production classes,
methods, and constructors have Javadoc; non-GUI line coverage is 99.2%.
